clips.text: He walks into a job interview — suit pressed, smile ready, every single answer rehearsed the night before.
The interviewer leans forward, looks him dead in the eye, and asks one question — the one question he was dreading all morning.
Did you really finish the project on time?
He didn't say a word. He didn't blink. He didn't even breathe. He just sat there.
But his skin had already answered — bright red, in front of everyone in the room, before his mouth could even open.
So how did she know he was lying? His skin answered before his mouth did — and it answers in two hundred milliseconds, every single time.
You wake up — and your skin is the colour of your bedsheets. The full story is on Ghazi What If — and it starts with a mirror.
